analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (Nov 23, 2026)
key_insights: US Market Intel moves back to Tactically Cautious after the bear case played out. SPX fell 8%, NDX 10% and RTY 7% in the Tech-induced selloff, and the desk admits it whiffed on the tactical bullish call.
A tactical bounce is expected but a sustainable rally is doubted. 2018 is seen as the best historical comp, where the late-year bounce was faded, and further rotation away from Tech is anticipated.

NVDA is the catalyst for the current leg. Concerns include Singapore revenue (21.7% of total in 26Q2) as a possible China backdoor, an SEC accounting probe, a California probe covering potential criminal violations, and circular financing. The stock is down about 48% from highs.

Export license data: NVDA and AMD requested 3.4mm chips to China and about 879k were approved, including to Alibaba and Tencent. AMD's note flagged similar regulatory risk, so the market is testing every part of the AI supply chain.

Semis narrative: 2026 may be peak AI capex growth with a sharper slowdown than forecast. Headwinds are midterm-related legislative changes, power and construction bottlenecks, and financing limits. Trump said he would tax or block data centers built outside the US.

Cybersecurity: breaches (MSFT, UAL, banks, NSA) and the FBI ARTEX warning suggest AI offense exceeds defense, which could bring regulation. The JPM Security Software basket (JP2SESF) is up 23.0% since June 30 and is the favored way to hold Tech exposure.

Positioning is low but not yet at a buy trigger. US TPM is at the 13th percentile since 2015 with a 4wk change near -1z against a -1.5z trigger. HFs are estimated at -1.5% on the day, about -4% MTD, and the 5d move is the worst since Apr 7, 2025.

HF net selling is approaching extremes (about -2z over 20 days globally). Semis remain the most net-sold US group over two months, while buying favored Utilities, Telecom, Pharma and Real Estate. Staples Distribution positioning is at historical highs.

Monetization Menu (Nov 23): market-neutral. Mag7 and Security Software are safest in Tech, with squeeze risk in Memory and Semis (use options). Long SPW vs short SPX or NDX, UK and EU to outperform, and Value to beat Beta and Momentum.

JPM x-asset view: the Fed is expected to hike three times (Dec, Jan, Mar) to 4.50-4.75% after hawkish October minutes. 2027 real GDP is 1.9% Q4/Q4 and core PCE settles near 2.5% in 2H27. Holds 2s/5s flatteners, is long USD, long AUD and NOK vs EUR and SEK, and prefers high-quality credit.

Desk color is bearish-leaning. Ron Adler sees no reason to buy the tape. Ilan Benhamou says the market is pricing a Fed policy error, expects an orderly SDVD wash-out as in 2022, and does not call to buy the dip. Marissa Gilter calls it a fear-led, not credit-led drawdown and says credit is the key tell.

Technicals: SPX first support is 7000-7100, with 6300 as the stronger support. DSI is at 10% bulls (capitulation). Short-term resistance is 7350-7415 and a close above confirms a bottom, with 7500-7600 a barrier. NDX, SMH and RSP have lower retracement supports 10-20% below.

Gold is selling off despite a lower dollar, lower real rates and higher equity vol, which has happened only 4x since 2000. Henrici speculates a possible Russia return to SWIFT on peace headlines as a driver of weakness, and sees a cash-raise pattern.

Consumer and economy remain resilient. Card spending grew 10% YoY at JPM and 13% at C, delinquencies are falling, and WMT cites over $2bn of incremental diesel costs. SPX 26Q3 median earnings growth was about 12%.

Dubravko reiterates SPX YE26 target of 8,000 (EPS $365, 21.9x), 8.4% upside. Ideas are long 12M vs short 3M Momentum, AI upstream attractive after the positioning flush, Low Vol less compelling, and Consumer Cyclicals challenged by affordability.
Market is not publishing Nov 25-27 and returns Nov 30. Key near-term events are PCE on Nov 25, ISM on Dec 1, NFP on Dec 4, FOMC on Dec 9, CPI on Dec 10, and the government funding deadline on Dec 11.

market_movers.rationale: Regulatory, SEC accounting and Singapore revenue concerns plus export licensing leave the stock down about 48% from highs with unclear support. Premarket it is up 8%.
Last week's AMD note flagged similar regulatory risks to NVDA for chip sales to Chinese entities.
Dubravko reiterates the 8,000 SPX YE26 target on $365 EPS at 21.9x.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically cautious. Mag7 and Security Software are safest, while Memory and Semis carry squeeze risk and uncertainty on NVDA persists.
A tilt to Cyclicals is favored if the economy holds up, particularly names insulated from the AI supply chain.
Expected to outperform on Cyclical and Value exposure, especially if the Dollar sees profit-taking.
Value to outperform Beta and Momentum.
Most net-sold US group, with peak capex concerns, though the JPM x-asset note sees relative value in memory and select semis.
Dubravko finds Low Vol less compelling but prefers Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples, within it.

earnings_insights: Nvidia 3Q results were strong with better-than-expected 4Q guidance per the JPM x-asset note, with risks around CEO succession and regulation.
SPX median earnings growth for 26Q3 was about 12% (reported, per FactSet), versus the 10-year average of 12.6%. Median profit margins hit fresh all-time highs.
NVDA 26Q2 Singapore revenue was $10.2bn (+81% YoY, reported), or 21.7% of total revenue of $46.7bn.
WMT said it will navigate over $2bn in incremental diesel and transportation costs this year. TGT and WMT described consumers as stable and resilient.
Upcoming earnings: DELL (Nov 24), CRWD and MRVL (Dec 1), CRM (Dec 2), AVGO (Dec 9), ORCL (Dec 10), MU (Dec 17). Today's reports are A, FLNC, HPE, SMTC and ZM.
Dubravko's SPX YE26 EPS estimate is $365 (forecast).

risk_factors: Further AI and Tech leg lower and a decline in the incremental buyer.
Hawkish Fed narrative and a possible December pivot to consecutive hikes.
Regulatory and legal risk for NVDA and AMD, including export controls and the SEC probe.
Hyperscaler capex uncertainty for 2027 and data center policy backlash.
Positioning purge and liquidity gaps from de-grossing of crowded themes.
Cyber attacks and outages from AI-enabled tools.
Credit rolling over would turn the de-gross into a growth scare.
Hormuz escalation and fuel cost pressure.
charts_described: NVDA price vs net income chart accompanies the NVDA discussion (no values in text).
Weekly Craig Cohen support charts: SPX first support 7000/7100 with 6300 stronger, NDX 38.2% retracement near 23,370 about 10% lower, RSP supports 3%, 7% (about 195) and 10% lower.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 30.18 and index realized vol closed about 24 (88th percentile on 5y) as of Friday.
Gilter: the share of market vol explained by macro factors jumped while stock-specific risk fell. Dealers are locally long gamma pinning TY, but a further rally would flip them short gamma.
Benhamou: going lower with lower implied vol is the only trade he wants. He expects an SDVD (spot down, vol down) wash-out rather than a vol spike.
US TPM at the 13th percentile since 2015. HF net leverage at the 26th percentile over 5 years, and global positioning around the 10th percentile and -1.5z.
Retail sentiment at YTD lows near Liberation Day levels. SPX is below its 200-day moving average and DSI is at 10% bulls.
Squeeze risk in Memory and Semis, so use options to play a rebound. Memory and Neoclouds are nearing consensus short.
geopolitical: Strait of Hormuz escalation risk: Iran trying to break a blockade and the US promising to sink ships.
US midterm outcomes (the 'Blue Wave') and its effect on data center capex legislation.
US export licenses for Nvidia and AMD chips to China, including Alibaba and Tencent, and Beijing not approving large-scale imports.
Trump said he and Xi agreed on joint AI guardrails. The US-China trade truce is extended through Jan 20, 2027.
Potential Russia-Ukraine peace and Russia's return to SWIFT as a gold headwind.
The UAE is shuttling oil past Iran in Hormuz. The US government funding deadline is Dec 11 and the G20 is Dec 15-16 in Miami.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is low, sentiment is at capitulation levels (DSI 10% bulls), HFs are cutting net risk at a magnitude historically followed by a bounce, and earnings growth is about 12%.
tension_points.bear_case: The 2018 analog suggests late-year bounces get faded. NVDA regulatory uncertainty, Fed hikes, and 2027-2028 capex opacity keep Tech longs risky, and positioning has not hit a buy trigger.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close above 7350-7415 on the SPX would confirm a short-term bottom, while a break below 7000 would invalidate the support view.

tension_points.bull_case: A dovish, patient December Fed with downside inflation surprises would support equities.
tension_points.bear_case: The October minutes guide to at least a 25bp hike and JPM expects three consecutive hikes, which would pressure financial conditions and credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A December pivot validating consecutive hikes would invalidate the constructive cyclicals call.
